transcript: Vulture recently put out a list called The Best Plays and musicals of 2025, which notably contained no musicals. It featured two different lists by reviewers Sarah Holden and Jackson McHenry, each giving their top 10 of the year. And you can pause to read, but I will put Sarah's list here and Jackson's list here. And as I mentioned at the top, despite its title, there is not a single musical on the list. And I am of a couple different minds about this. Number one, they probably could have given us a musical. There have certainly been several musicals this year that I think are deserving of a top 10 best of the year list. Just off the top of my head, we had Off Broadway, Mexitus, Beau, of course, masquerade. And then on Broadway, we had Real Women have Curves, uh, Buena Vista, Social Club, and I really love two strangers carry a cake across New York, which just opened. Let's not to begrudge any of the plays that they did pick. I think they are all great choices and deserving in their own right. And I know firsthand how hard it can be to produce a top 10 list with so many great shows to choose from. I just think with the title The Best Plays and musicals of 2025, you could have thrown us a bone and given us at least one musical. However, I also think, objectively, it has been a much better year for Plays than it has been for musicals. And if anything, these lists kind of serve as an indictment on the current state of musical theater, which has been a bit of a mixed bag, to put it lightly. And part of that is, I think that we're not seeing producers take big swings in the types of musicals they're producing, particularly new musicals. I do think that is true of plays as well, at least on Broadway. But plays have a couple of benefits. Number one, they're much cheaper to produce. Number two, it's much easier to get a celebrity to come to your play on Broadway than it is your musical. And 3, the infrastructure to present new plays off Broadway is just much stronger than it is to present new musicals. But it is LED to this environment where I think plays are really thriving and musicals are starting to struggle. That is definitely impacted the quality of the output. Like, I am working on my own list of 10 best musicals and 10 best plays of the year. I have plays that I really loved that I don't think are gonna make my top 10, because there's so many great choices. And then on the musical side, I really struggled to fill all 10 slots, if I'm being honest. Again, I don't want to imply that there are no good musicals happening. There absolutely are. But I do think that we are in a golden age for Plays. And we are not seeing that same success in musical theater
